title: 02 · Active profiles decided per environment at startup
question: The app has dynamic active profiles that vary by environment/index and can't be fixed at build time. Spring AOT runs at build time; does that freeze the profiles?

answer.pass: Profiles and everything that is a value are decided at startup, even with Spring AOT: one image became dev1, dev2, qa1 and prod1 with the right profiles, profile-file values and @Bean-method choice, and every environment used the same JDK AOT cache (trained with no profile active) and started as fast as prod1. What Spring AOT freezes is which beans exist: the @Profile("prod") and @ConditionalOnProperty beans were missing in prod with AOT on and only appeared when the same image ran without Spring AOT, which also started measurably slower. So vary values per environment, never the bean graph.
answer.fail: Not as expected: at least one result differs from the known behaviour. See 'Unexpected results' for what differed and what to check.
answer.inconclusive: Probably, but some startup times varied too much between runs to be sure. Close other workloads and rerun with more runs (make examples EX=02 RUNS=10).

tested: One image (profiles-app) built with Spring AOT and no profile active at build time.

Six instances of it: dev1, dev2, qa1, prod1 (profiles from APP_ENV + APP_ENV_INDEX), prod1 plus SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=debug, and prod1 without Spring AOT (same image and JDK AOT cache, minus Spring AOT's generated bean code).
For each: active profiles, values from application-<profile>.yml, which Notifier the @Bean method chose, and whether the two pitfall beans exist (@Profile("prod") and @ConditionalOnProperty).

Then each instance again on its own: once with class-load logging, to count how many classes came from the JDK AOT cache (trained in the build with no profile active), and RUNS times to time Spring's startup (median reported).

started.label: started
started.why: Every instance is the same image with valid settings.
ifUnexpected: Look at the container log in the evidence file.
Is the image built? make -C examples/02-dynamic-profiles image

aot.label: Spring AOT generated code in use
aot.why: The image starts with -Dspring.aot.enabled=true; 'prod1 without Spring AOT' overrides the entrypoint without it (but keeps the JDK AOT cache).
ifUnexpected: Check the image's ENTRYPOINT (docker image inspect) still passes -Dspring.aot.enabled=true.

profiles.label: active profiles
profiles.why: EnvironmentProfilesPostProcessor (common/) turns APP_ENV + APP_ENV_INDEX into '<env>,<env><index>' at startup, before config files load. Profiles from SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE are kept and go last, so they override.
ifUnexpected: Is EnvironmentProfilesPostProcessor registered? (common/src/main/resources/META-INF/spring.factories)
Check the instance's APP_ENV / APP_ENV_INDEX in the evidence (startup log).

db-name.label: app.db-name (from application-<env>.yml)
db-name.why: Profile-specific files are read at startup, so each environment gets its own values even though the image is the same.
ifUnexpected: Did the profiles come out right? The value follows the profile.
Check the application-<profile>.yml files in the app's resources.

notifier.label: notifier (@Bean method)
notifier.why: The AOT-safe pattern: one bean definition fixed at build time; its method body runs at startup and picks Log/Email/PagerNotifier from app.notifier.
ifUnexpected: Check app.notifier in the profile files, and NotifierConfig.

pitfall.profile.nonprod.label: @Profile("prod") bean exists
pitfall.profile.nonprod.why: Not prod, so the bean is absent with or without AOT. This instance doesn't show the limitation.
ifUnexpected: The bean exists outside prod: check ProdOnlyAuditor's @Profile.

pitfall.conditional.nonprod.label: @ConditionalOnProperty bean exists
pitfall.conditional.nonprod.why: app.fancy-feature is false outside prod, so the bean is absent with or without AOT.
ifUnexpected: Check app.fancy-feature in the non-prod profile files.

pitfall.profile.aot.label: @Profile("prod") bean exists
pitfall.profile.aot.why: Spring AOT evaluated @Profile once, at build time, when no profile was active, so the bean isn't in the generated bean graph. In prod, where it 'should' exist, it doesn't. Don't use @Profile to vary beans per environment with AOT.
ifUnexpected: If the bean exists, Spring AOT probably isn't active: check the 'Spring AOT generated code in use' check for this instance.
Or the image was built with the prod profile active during process-aot.

pitfall.conditional.aot.label: @ConditionalOnProperty bean exists
pitfall.conditional.aot.why: application-prod.yml sets app.fancy-feature=true, but Spring AOT evaluated the condition at build time, when it was false. A runtime property can't add or remove a bean under AOT.
ifUnexpected: If the bean exists, Spring AOT probably isn't active: check the 'Spring AOT generated code in use' check for this instance.

pitfall.profile.noaot.label: @Profile("prod") bean exists
pitfall.profile.noaot.why: Contrast: without Spring AOT, Spring evaluates @Profile at startup, so the prod bean appears. That's what people expect, and why the AOT behaviour surprises them.
ifUnexpected: Check this instance really ran without AOT (its 'Spring AOT generated code in use' check).

pitfall.conditional.noaot.label: @ConditionalOnProperty bean exists
pitfall.conditional.noaot.why: Contrast: without Spring AOT the condition is evaluated at startup against application-prod.yml, so the bean appears.
ifUnexpected: Check this instance really ran without AOT (its 'Spring AOT generated code in use' check).

cache.dev1.label: JDK AOT cache used
cache.dev1.why: The JDK AOT cache was trained in the image build with no profile active. It depends on the JDK, the classpath and the JVM flags, not on profiles or config files, so every environment uses it. Classes the training run never loaded come from the jar as usual.
ifUnexpected: If every instance shows 'not used', the image was built for another CPU architecture or JDK: rebuild it (make -C examples/02-dynamic-profiles image).
Read the JVM's own message in the evidence file (from -Xlog:aot).

cache.prod1-no-spring-aot.label: JDK AOT cache used
cache.prod1-no-spring-aot.why: The JDK AOT cache doesn't depend on Spring AOT: the JDK, classpath and JVM flags are the same, so the JVM uses it. Without Spring AOT, Spring loads extra classes to process the configuration at startup; those weren't in the training run and come from the jar. So this instance's startup differs from prod1 only by Spring AOT.
ifUnexpected: Read the JVM's own message in the evidence file (from -Xlog:aot).
Check that demo.sh still starts this instance with -XX:AOTCache=/app/app.aot.

dev1.label: dev1
dev1.why: Same image, JVM flags and JDK AOT cache as prod1. Only the profiles and the config files they load differ, which costs nothing measurable.

dev2.label: dev2
dev2.why: Same image, JVM flags and JDK AOT cache as prod1. Only the profiles and the config files they load differ, which costs nothing measurable.

qa1.label: qa1
qa1.why: Same image, JVM flags and JDK AOT cache as prod1. Only the profiles and the config files they load differ, which costs nothing measurable.

prod1.label: prod1
prod1.why: What Spring AOT is worth here: the same image and JDK AOT cache without Spring AOT is slower, because Spring then parses the configuration classes and evaluates their conditions at every startup. That is what you get in exchange for the bean graph being fixed at build time.
ifUnexpected: Check the 'Spring AOT generated code in use' checks: true for prod1, false for prod1 without Spring AOT.
Was something else running? Check `make status`, then rerun with RUNS=10.

prod1-debug.label: prod1 + debug profile
prod1-debug.why: An operator-added profile is one more config file to read: no measurable cost.

prod1-no-spring-aot.label: prod1 without Spring AOT
prod1-no-spring-aot.why: Reference: prod1 from the same image, still with the JDK AOT cache, but without Spring AOT's generated bean code.
